text:
incident-bot: P2 alert: customer-facing quality regression detected for tenant `acme-health-prod` in Dedicated Pool `dedicated-42`. Degraded BLEU/ROUGE on evaluation set, request rate 600rps -> small spike in errors. Paging on-call.

michelle (on-call): on it. saw the alert, joining. what metric triggered?

incident-bot: Regression detector triggered on `rl_evals/weekly/promoted_prompts` and production sampling checks. Quality delta: -12% avg likelihood, -23% automated eval score vs baseline.

raj (eng-ml): i’m looking. initial hypothesis: last night’s quantization profile change rolled out to tenant variant `gpt-3.5-redwood-q4_0` -> likely precision loss at certain prompt patterns.

leo (eng-runtime): confirming: deployment history shows a profile tweak rolled at 2026-03-25T02:13Z to `q4_0` for pool `dedicated-42` to improve throughput. rollback is possible.

sara (cs): customer is in the middle of a live demo in EMEA, flagged latency okay but answers are hallucinating more. they already pinged our support on-call. i can be the customer point. need ETA to fix.

michelle (on-call): thanks. priority = P2 (customer-visible non-blocking but urgent). plan options: (A) revert quantization profile for acme-health to previous `fp16` variant (fast, known good), (B) switch tenant to hosted-compatible variant fallback (slightly higher cost), (C) patch model to skip last-layer quantization (risky).

raj (eng-ml): recommending A then B if issues persist. rollback procedure: update tenant model variant mapping to `model:v1.12.3-fp16` and restart workers for that tenant. Doing a canary to 5% traffic for 10m.

leo (eng-runtime): i'll run the rollback steps. will coordinate with ops for pool restarts if needed. executing safe canary via `rwinfctl` (internal tooling).

ops: standing by for restart window. note: rollback may bump GPU memory usage by ~18% on `dedicated-42`. need to ensure no OOMs.

michelle (on-call): post the rollback command and canary plan here. include runbook bits.

raj (eng-ml): command to change variant mapping (internal CLI):

```
# canary 5% -> 10m
rwinfctl tenant update-variant --tenant acme-health-prod \
  --pool dedicated-42 \
  --from-variant gpt-3.5-redwood-q4_0 \
  --to-variant model:v1.12.3-fp16 \
  --canary 0.05 --canary-duration 10m
```

After canary, promote with `--canary 1.0` to shift 100% if metrics look good.

leo (eng-runtime): running canary now. tailing logs.

```
[2026-03-25T08:22:11Z] rwinfctl: canary start tenant=acme-health-prod pool=dedicated-42 to=model:v1.12.3-fp16 canary=5%
[2026-03-25T08:23:05Z] runtime: allocated 2 extra fp16 contexts to pool dedicated-42
[2026-03-25T08:25:30Z] perf: latency +6% p50, p95 unchanged; token cost +12%
[2026-03-25T08:29:10Z] quality-check: sample-batch eval_loss delta -0.02 (improvement)
```

leo (eng-runtime): canary looks stable. no OOMs. p50 latency up ~40ms but within SLO.

raj (eng-ml): running automated eval suite (`rl_evals/production/smoke`) on canary outputs. initial numbers are back to baseline on 3/4 prompt groups. running additional edge-case checks.

sara (cs): telling customer we have rolled back a perf optimization and are monitoring; will follow up in 15m with update. suggested customer message:

"Hi — we detected a model quality regression and have temporarily reverted a change for your dedicated environment to restore expected output quality. We're monitoring and will update within 15 minutes. Apologies for the disruption to your demo. — Sara, Redwood Support"

michelle (on-call): good. keep me posted. if automated evals pass, promote to 100% traffic. timeline target: 30m from now to full rollback and customer confirmation.

leo (eng-runtime): promoting to 100% now:
```
rwinfctl tenant update-variant --tenant acme-health-prod --pool dedicated-42 --to-variant model:v1.12.3-fp16 --canary 1.0
```
[2026-03-25T08:41:02Z] runtime: promo complete -> 100% traffic on fp16 variant for acme-health-prod

michelle (on-call): monitoring metrics dashboard: quality metrics trending back to baseline, error rate steady. sara please confirm customer sees expected behavior.

sara (cs): customer confirms responses quality restored, demo resumed. they asked for root-cause timeline and preventive steps.

raj (eng-ml): root cause: quantization profile `q4_0` reduced precision on a small subset of tokens used heavily by this tenant's prompts (medical abbreviations) leading to semantic errors in completion. Rollout gating missed because our automated eval suite didn't include tenant-specific prompt set.

michelle (on-call): actions: 1) immediate: keep fp16 variant for acme-health-prod until we validate revised quantization (DONE). 2) short-term: add tenant-specific eval prompts to smoke tests for acme-health-prod (raj+cs). 3) medium: add rollout gating rule to require tenant-similarity checks for quantization changes (eng-runtime + eng-ml). 4) follow-up: postmortem and customer blameless writeup (owner: michelle).

raj (eng-ml): i'll prepare a guarded q4 tweak with token-importance weighting and test on canary tenant copies. will ping when ready.

leo (eng-runtime): logging notes for postmortem: pool dedicated-42 had an automated `perf-opt` job that applied the `q4_0` profile to tenants matching `perf-tier:high`. we should decouple perf-opt from tenant-specific tags.

ops: noted. increase monitoring retention for this tenant by 72h to capture edge cases.

michelle (on-call): leaving a handoff note for next shift (tagging oncall): keep fp16 variant until further notice, watch `quality.delta` and `errors.rate`. Postmortem draft in `#postmortems` by EOD.

incident-bot: incident resolved -> severity downgraded, customer confirmed remediation. ticket: INC-2026-3219.

sara (cs): will follow up with customer with a timeline and offer a dedicated post-incident review.

michelle (on-call): great work team. closing thread after postmortem + runbook updates.
